name: BPH6
question: How does prostatic urethral lift compare with transurethral resection of the prostate for symptom relief, recovery, sexual function, continence, and safety?

design.population: Men with BPH-related lower urinary tract symptoms who were candidates for TURP, aged at least 50 years, with IPSS above 12, Qmax at most 15 mL/s, and prostate volume at most 60 cc.
design.locator: Sønksen 2015, PubMed abstract, Methods; Gratzke 2017, full text, Study Protocol and Procedure

verdictNote: The novel BPH6 composite favored PUL; later symptom and flow gains favored TURP.
takeaway: Prostatic urethral lift was noninferior and superior to TURP on the 12-month BPH6 composite responder endpoint; both relieved symptoms, while lift favored ejaculation preservation and recovery.

reports.label: 12-month primary report
reports.citation: Sønksen J, Barber NJ, Speakman MJ, et al. "Prospective, Randomized, Multinational Study of Prostatic Urethral Lift Versus Transurethral Resection of the Prostate: 12-month Results from the BPH6 Study." *Eur Urol.* 2015;68(4):643-652. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2015.04.024

results.measure: 12-month composite of symptom relief, recovery, erectile and ejaculatory preservation, continence preservation, and safety
results.note: The abstract reports both noninferiority and superiority of PUL; it gives no arm-specific responder rates or confidence limit.
results.locator: PubMed abstract, Outcome Measurements and Results

results.endpoint: Ejaculatory function preservation and quality of recovery
results.note: Both favored PUL; the abstract does not give arm-specific rates.

reports.label: 2-year follow-up
reports.citation: Gratzke C, Barber N, Speakman MJ, et al. "Prostatic urethral lift vs transurethral resection of the prostate: 2-year results of the BPH6 prospective, multicentre, randomized study." *BJU Int.* 2017;119(5):767-775. doi:10.1111/bju.13714
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Study Protocol and Procedure; Table 1

results.measure: Patients with a quality-of-recovery visual analogue score of at least 70/100 by 1 month
results.note: The article does not give the denominators for these percentages.
results.locator: Full text, Results, paragraph before Table 1

results.measure: Mean paired change from baseline at 24 months; a larger reduction favors TURP
results.note: Nominal between-arm P value; not significant after the paper's Hochberg multiple-testing correction.

results.measure: Mean paired change in maximum flow from baseline at 24 months; a larger increase favors TURP
results.note: Nominal between-arm P value; not significant after the paper's Hochberg multiple-testing correction.

results.measure: Mean paired change in ejaculatory function score at 24 months; a higher score favors PUL
results.note: Between-arm comparison; ejaculatory bother did not differ significantly.
results.locator: Full text, Table 1, MSHQ-EjD function and bother, 24 months

results.measure: Patients with at least the study's minimal clinically important difference at 24 months
results.note: The threshold was borrowed from a urinary incontinence population; the between-arm difference was not statistically significant.
results.locator: Full text, Patients and Methods, SF-6D MCID paragraph; Table 2, 24 months

delivery.label: PUL technique
delivery.value: Transurethral permanent UroLift implants compressed prostatic tissue to enlarge the urethral lumen without resection or thermal injury.
delivery.locator: Full text, Introduction and Study Protocol and Procedure

delivery.label: Operator experience and TURP technique
delivery.value: Investigators had performed 0–20 PUL procedures before study start; each had extensive TURP experience and used their usual TURP practice.
